text:
Dear Winnie,

Thanks for your email.

As mentioned in our Slack group, I have scheduled our next call for tomorrow morning your time. In the meantime, please allow me to share our detailed findings & cost estimate for your review: -

Project Overview:

The task involves reviewing the video and adding captions for each action performed within the clip. Each caption must clearly describe the hand involved, the action being performed, and the object associated with the action. The captions should accurately represent the sequence of actions observed in the video while maintaining consistency in terminology and description format.

Key Challenges:

*	Videos with repeated actions are easier and faster to process, while videos containing multiple actions and objects require additional review time and careful observation.
*	Actions involving multiple objects require more detailed captions to accurately describe the hand movement, action, and associated objects.
*	Some objects are difficult to identify due to low video quality, motion blur, partial visibility, occlusion, lighting conditions, or similarity between objects, which increases validation time.
*	Rapid hand movements, overlapping actions, or simultaneous actions performed by both hands increase task complexity and require frame-by-frame review.
*	Maintaining consistency in caption structure, object naming, and action terminology across all videos requires additional quality checks and attention during processing.
*	Understanding and becoming familiar with the functionality of the tool.

Skill sets required:

As we have involved 2 junior and 2 senior text annotators on the free POC stage, we have found that it is difficult to expect the right level of productivity and accuracy from junior annotators. We need a mix of mid-level and senior annotators for your project. By doing this, we can expect the necessary quality standards in your project.

subject: Re: Encord project
text:
Hi Stewart,

Great speaking with you and the team as well. 6/15 @10am PT should work for a follow-up.

I’ve attached v1.4 of the Collection Spec to this email which relaxes and clarifies a number of requirements. The main changes are:

Segment Duration/Timestamps

  *   We have updated the frame tolerance from ±3 frames to ±5 frames.
  *   We will now audit at frame-level precision only for contact-demarcated segment boundaries (i.e. contact-based starts and ends). Please see the visual in the spec for an example of how a densely segmented section would be audited.
  *   For segment duration, each segment should ideally capture one discrete action. However, when actions are extremely short, seamless, or difficult to segment reliably (such as in the case or coordinated two-handed actions), a single segment may include up to 3 discrete actions. This flexibility is intended to preserve annotation reliability while still capturing the relevant action structure. Segments should generally remain under 10 seconds.

Coordinated Two-Handed Actions

  *   If one hand is not meaningfully related to the work being performed, it does not need to be annotated. For example, stabilizing a task-relevant object may need to be described, while simply resting a hand on the table does not.
  *   The segment should span the earliest action-intent from either hand to the latest action-intent from either hand (e.g., when opening a jar, the segment begins the moment the left hand reaches to stabilize the base and ends the moment the right hand finishes pulling the lid away.)

Other Updates

  *   We have removed walking / general bodily movement from the label requirements.
  *   When there are more than 3 indistinguishable similar objects, object-level disambiguation is not required.

Let me know if you have any questions!
Anna

subject: Re: Follow Up to our Discussion- Encord
text:
Hi Zachary,

 I gave Claude Code Label Studio's React plugin documentation page and then
told it to create the UI there.
Then it coded out and pushed the changes there. I tested the UI and then
told Claude some bugs and then it fixed directly.
I never looked into the source code directly as the UI will be only facing
annotators and annotators will also report issue to me so all these changes
are very low risk.

It supported drawing table boundary lines pretty easily and I can multi
select the grids to create merge cells easily. I then created Excel like
interaction page pretty easily too where I can copy paste and modify bulk
number of table cells.
Maintenance is pretty easy since I just rely on vibe code and the risk of
breaking is very low.

Beyond parsing UI, we care about for managing different roles for
annotators and controlling their access on data.

Given Label Studio gives full flexibility on code, what matters the most is
if Encord can match this feature.
I can build any UI without needing any front end engineer or ask infra
engineer on deployment which is super handy for MLE to iterate fast and
experiment on different ways of annotating
I can instantly apply changes that annotators flagged.

But something I think Encord could be better is the support and
responsivensss. Given it was really difficult to get Label Studio's
attention, we find that part a risk.

Best,
Joon
